item.title: Designed multiple sequence alignments guide AlphaFold for improved modeling of loop-mediated protein-protein interactions.
item.abstract: Accurate modeling of synthetic protein-protein interactions is essential for designing therapeutics, diagnostics, and molecular imaging reagents. Although deep learning has transformed protein structure prediction, modeling heteromeric interactions mediated by flexible loops-as in antibodies, nanobodies, and monobodies-remains challenging due to weak coevolutionary signals at binding interfaces and substantial conformational variability. Here, we present a framework that guides AlphaFold predictions of loop-mediated interactions using synthetic multiple sequence alignments (MSAs) generated through ProteinMPNN interface design. Benchmarks across nanobody-, antibody-, and monobody-antigen complexes show that designed MSAs encode interface-specific contact information that can be leveraged in two complementary ways. First, AlphaFold2-Multimer and AlphaFold3 predictions conditioned on designed MSAs produce confident and accurate structures for compatible interfaces, while yielding low-confidence or structurally inconsistent predictions for incompatible sequences or docking poses, enabling improved evaluation of candidate protein-protein complex models-particularly relevant for protein design. Second, when applied to AlphaFold-predicted structures, designed MSAs guide structural refinement and reranking, enabling the development of a strategy that improves blind structure prediction in low-confidence cases without exhaustive sampling. Together, these results establish designed MSAs as controllable inputs for structure prediction, with applications in protein design and blind prediction of challenging protein-protein interactions.

item.title: Integrative Genomic and Stem Cell Frameworks for Variant-to-Function Discovery in Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Narrative Review.
item.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition shaped by de novo protein-truncating variants, inherited missense substitutions, recurrent copy number variations (CNVs), and distributed polygenic risk. These alterations converge on a limited set of neurobiological processes, including synaptic refinement, excitation-to-inhibition balance, chromatin state regulation, and glial-mediated neuroimmune signaling. Experimental paradigms now exist for systematic variant-to-function interrogation through CRISPR-engineered isogenic human pluripotent stem-cell libraries incorporating Cas9 nucleases, programmable transcriptional modulators (dCas9-KRAB and dCas9-VP64), base editors, and prime editing systems. Coupled with single-cell multi-omic platforms such as Perturb-seq, scATAC-seq, and CITE-seq, and with circuit-level phenotyping through multielectrode arrays, calcium imaging, and quantitative morphometry, these systems resolve ASD-relevant cellular states at single-cell and cell-type-specific resolution. In this narrative review, we distinguish deliberately between what these platforms have already established and what remains proposed. To date, a small number of studies constitute the demonstrated evidence base: in vivo Perturb-seq of 35 ASD/neurodevelopmental risk genes in mouse cortex, mosaic knockout of ASD genes in human cortical organoids, the CHOOSE organoid screen of 36 risk genes, assembloid CRISPR screening of 425 neurodevelopmental-disorder risk genes, a 63-line mouse embryonic stem-cell CNV resource, and a CRISPRi screen of 102 ASD risk genes in human induced pluripotent stem-cell (iPSC)-derived microglia implicating ADNP in synaptic pruning. We summarized these in a dedicated comparison table. Against this, integration of polygenic and noncoding architecture, causal-inference frameworks, such as Mendelian randomization and do-calculus, and cross-laboratory reproducibility, remain aspirational rather than realized. We therefore frame the field's principal near-term requirement not as further gene discovery but as harmonized protocols, shared reference lines, arrayed validation capacity, and interpretable statistical frameworks capable of converting perturbation atlases into causal mechanism.

item.title: Photoswitchable optoGPCRs for reversible control of Gs signalling and arrestin recruitment
item.abstract: OptoGPCRs are light-activatable G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) used to optogenetically control physiological processes. Most existing optoGPCRs are based on monostable opsins, which are limited by photobleaching and irreversibility. The bistable jumping spider rhodopsin 1 (JSR1) carrying the single point mutant S199F introduces a ~150 nm spectral separation between the active and inactive states, enabling bidirectional control with distinct wavelengths of light. Here, we show that JSR1-S199F robustly and reversibly recruits arrestin and modulates Gq/i protein activity. We then engineered JSR1-S199F-based optoGPCRs with Gs protein activity, guided by AlphaFold-predicted receptor-miniGs complexes, to expand the limited repertoire of bistable Gs-coupled optoGPCRs. Specifically, we present optoDRD1, a chimeric optoGPCR that redirects the native Gq/i protein activity of JSR1 towards the Gs pathway of the dopamine D1 receptor (DRD1). Through systematic screening of intracellular domain combinations, we identified a chimeric configuration with the highest absolute cAMP output comprising ICL2, ICL3, helix 8, and the C-terminus from DRD1. The resulting optoGPCR is activated by violet light ({lambda}max = 397 nm) and deactivated by green light ({lambda}max = 531 nm) at physiologically relevant light intensities. A single violet light pulse drives sustained Gs signalling for several hours, while green light rapidly deactivates the receptor at any chosen time point, enabling repeatable switching between active and inactive states over multiple cycles. OptoDRD1 closely mimics wild-type DRD1 in both cAMP signalling kinetics and G protein selectivity, with a signal amplitude comparable to native Gs-coupled receptors, including JellyOp. We further demonstrate optoDRD1's utility for optogenetic control of Gs-regulated processes in vitro, including insulin secretion in human {beta}-cells and signalling modulation in a neuronal cell line. The biochemical stability and known structure of JSR1 make it a robust scaffold for this rational engineering and for future biophysical characterization. Together, optoDRD1 and JSR1-S199F expand the optoGPCR toolkit and open new opportunities for dissecting dopaminergic signalling, Gs-mediated physiology, and GPCR signalling pharmacology.

item.title: An AI-designed, recombinantly produced FtsZ-directed peptide with in vitro activity against pan-drug-resistant clinical isolates.
item.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance is outpacing the antibiotic pipeline, yet antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) - the most-cited alternative class - remain constrained by proteolytic instability, host toxicity, and the cost of solid-phase synthesis. We report an integrated design-to-validation pipeline that addresses these constraints and yields a de novo peptide directed at an intracellular, non-lytic target. Instead of relying on membrane disruption, the design was directed at FtsZ, the essential bacterial cell-division GTPase, at a consensus epitope (residues 60-145) that our alignments show is substantially more conserved across the Gram-positive/Gram-negative divide than FtsZ overall (68.6% versus 50.1% identity between Enterococcus and Klebsiella orthologues) while sharing only approximately 8-24% identity with human tubulin. A sequence-space diffusion model conditioned on the amino-acid composition of experimentally validated AMPs generated ten binders; fusion to 120 cell-penetrating motifs, machine-learning triage, co-folding and replicated molecular dynamics identified a single lead, Combined111. Rather than chemical synthesis, the peptide was produced biologically: the codon-optimised gene was cloned in-house into pHT254 and expressed as an intracellular, C-terminal 8xHis-tagged product in the protease-deficient Bacillus subtilis WB800N host, giving a mean transcript induction of 3.40-fold (SD 2.01, n = 4 biological replicates) and a single band of approximately 11.1 kDa after one-step Ni-NTA purification. Against one pan-drug-resistant clinical isolate of each of seven species, the purified peptide produced larger inhibition zones than a panel of last-resort antibiotics for five of the seven, by a mean of 4.81 mm, although this difference was not statistically significant (95% CI -0.64 to 10.27; t(6) = 2.16, p = 0.074, Cohen's dz = 0.82). Each zone value is a single measurement, so reproducibility was not assessed, and inhibition-zone diameters are not a direct measure of comparative potency. The advantage was consistent in direction but not uniform, the pan-drug-resistant Enterococcus faecalis isolate being the least susceptible. E. faecium FtsZ was the sequence used for the computational design, whereas the Gram-positive organism available for experimental testing was E. faecalis. These findings show that generative design can be coupled to low-cost bacterial expression in one laboratory. FtsZ-directed inhibition is presented here as a hypothesis rather than an established mechanism: target engagement was inferred from alignment, co-folding and molecular dynamics, and no direct binding measurement, FtsZ polymerisation or GTPase assay, or Z-ring localisation experiment was performed. Minimum inhibitory concentrations, resistance selection, haemolysis, mammalian cytotoxicity, and in vivo efficacy all remain to be established.

item.title: Cerebra: A computationally efficient framework for accurate protein structure prediction.
item.abstract: Remarkable progress has been made in the field of protein structure prediction. Representative methods like AlphaFold and RoseTTAFold achieve prediction accuracy close to experimental structural determination, but at the cost of heavy computational consumption for model training. In this work, we propose a new framework, Cerebra, for improving the computational efficiency of protein structure prediction. In this network architecture, multiple sets of atomic coordinates are predicted parallelly and their mutual complementarity is leveraged to rapidly improve the quality of predicted structures through a new attention mechanism named path synthesis attention (PSA). Consequently, Cerebra markedly reduces the computational consumption, achieving evident acceleration on both model training and inference, in comparison to OpenFold, the academic version of AlphaFold2. When evaluated on the CAMEO 2025 dataset, the Cerebra model trained on a limited number of GPUs shows comparable performance to the published OpenFold model that has been thoroughly optimized using a plethora of computational resources. Moreover, ablation studies confirm that the PSA mechanism efficiently accelerates the network convergence, suggesting its potential in handling the many-body effects of protein geometries in graph-based models. Finally, the fast inference of Cerebra effectively assists hallucination-based de novo protein backbone design, allowing the production of abundant backbone structures with sufficient designability and novelty.

item.title: Construction of a stable T7 expression system inSaccharomyces cerevisiae based on extranuclear replication system.
item.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The bacteriophage T7 expression system is a powerful tool for recombinant protein production, yet its application in eukaryotes is hindered by nuclear-cytoplasmic compartmentalization and inefficient mRNA export. To circumvent this barrier, we aimed to construct a stable cytoplasmic T7 expression system in Saccharomyces cerevisiae by utilizing the extranuclear replication system based on linear plasmids pGKL1/pGKL2 from Kluyveromyces lactis.
RESULTS: We integrated the T7 RNA polymerase gene under control of the constitutive TEF1 promoter into the genome of S. cerevisiae F102-2u, and inserted a T7 expression cassette containing an internal ribosome entry site (IRES) into the cytoplasmic p1 plasmid. The system achieved high-level expression of NanoLuc® luciferase (luminescence intensity ~ 108) comparable to the strong Gal system, and successfully expressed super-folder GFP. Quantitative analysis showed that T7 RNA polymerase exhibited higher transcription efficiency and greater processivity on the p1 plasmid compared to genomic DNA or the 2μ plasmid, with early-stage transcription being up to 100-fold higher than on genomic DNA. The system maintained stable expression over multiple passages under selective pressure.
CONCLUSION: This study establishes a robust cytoplasmic T7 expression system in yeast, resolving the nuclear export issue. It further demonstrates that higher-order DNA structure profoundly influences T7 transcription efficiency. This system provides a novel strategy for efficient protein production and has broad applications in synthetic biology and industrial biotechnology.

item.title: Connecting Chassis Metabolism with Glycosyltransferase Catalysis: The Role of Nucleotide Sugars in Human Milk Oligosaccharide Biosynthesis.
item.abstract: Nucleotide sugars connect host metabolism to glycosyltransferase(GT)-catalyzed human milk oligosaccharide (HMO) biosynthesis, yet larger donor pools do not necessarily increase product formation. This review examines GDP-fucose, UDP-N-acetylglucosamine, UDP-galactose, and CMP-N-acetylneuraminic acid in relation to precursor competition, nucleotide regeneration, catalytic performance, and host physiology. It distinguishes direct donor consumption from upstream precursor, energy, biomass, and maintenance requirements and compares fermentation, whole-cell conversion, and cell-free biocatalysis. Published studies show that production depends on coordination among donor formation, active GT capacity, acceptor accessibility, competing metabolism, and process conditions. Sampling and extraction artifacts can distort donor-pool estimates, while in vitro kinetic parameters may not predict performance in cellular systems. Manufacturing assessment also requires attention to catalyst lifetime, product recovery, structural quality, and scale-up. An experimental framework is proposed to guide measurements and independent perturbations of donor supply, GT activity, acceptor access, and transport. HMO production should be assessed by yield, productivity, selectivity, structural identity, and stability, rather than donor abundance or endpoint titer alone.

item.title: Astrocytic mitochondria restore neuronal bioenergetics and function in Parkinson disease models.
item.abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction contributes to neuronal injury in Parkinson's disease, and astrocyte-derived mitochondria may offer neuroprotection by restoring neuronal bioenergetics. Here, we investigated the therapeutic potential of astrocyte-derived mitochondria in 6-OHDA models of Parkinson's disease. Using mitochondrial labeling and co-culture assays, we obtained evidence consistent with the release of astrocytic mitochondria, their uptake by injured neurons, and their association with the neuronal mitochondrial network. Building on this observation, we investigated whether direct delivery of functional astrocytic mitochondria could augment endogenous support during neuronal injury. Infused astrocytic mitochondria reduced oxidative stress, restored mitochondrial membrane potential, improved mitochondrial respiration, normalized calcium homeostasis, reduced early neuronal apoptosis, and restored mitochondrial mass. Astrocytic mitochondrial delivery enhanced dendritic arborization in primary neurons. In vivo, stereotactic infusion restored TH immunoreactivity in the SNpc and improved motor and non-motor behavioral deficits. These findings support the potential of astrocyte-derived mitochondria as a promising cell-free therapeutic approach for Parkinson's disease.

item.title: From oil biosynthesis to precision breeding: Genetic improvement of fatty acid composition in oilseed crops.
item.abstract: Fatty acid composition is a major determinant of nutritional quality, oxidative stability and functional value of oilseed crops. It is shaped by coordinated plastidial fatty acid synthesis, endoplasmic reticulum-associated desaturation and elongation, acyl editing, triacylglycerol assembly and lipid turnover in seed. This review summarizes the metabolic basis of fatty acid diversity of edible oil in major and specialty oilseed crops, then examines how genetic architecture and omics-assisted discovery have accelerated the identification of loci, alleles and candidate genes controlling fatty acid composition. We emphasize a design framework that links locus discovery to allele prioritization, targeted editing, pathway engineering and field deployment. Linkage mapping, bulked segregant sequencing, genome wide association studies, transcriptomics, proteomics and pangenome analyses are increasingly revealing both canonical genes and previously unrecognized structural or regulatory variation. We further discuss improvement strategies ranging from conventional and marker-assisted breeding to single-gene editing, transgenic manipulation and multigene synthetic biology. Finally, we highlight emerging opportunities in population genomics, underutilized oil crop mining, artificial intelligence (AI)-guided enzyme and promoter design, and agronomic evaluation. Collectively, these advances are shifting oilseed improvement from empirical selection toward rational, pathway-informed design of fatty acid profiles, while emphasizing the continuing need for biochemical validation and field-level performance assessment.

item.title: Serial Tumor-Agnostic Plasma Profiling with a Compact NGS Panel During First-Line Therapy for Newly Diagnosed Metastatic Colorectal Cancer.
item.abstract: Plasma circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) profiling may complement tissue hotspot testing and reveal molecular changes during treatment of metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC). We prospectively studied 39 patients with newly diagnosed unresectable mCRC receiving first-line therapy. Cell-free DNA was collected before treatment and after two and four cycles and analyzed using a 10 kb, 10-gene hybrid-capture sequencing panel with molecular barcodes and error correction. Baseline oncogenic variants were detected in 32 of 35 evaluable patients (91.4%). Compared with routine tissue PCR for shared RAS/BRAF targets, plasma testing showed 84.2% sensitivity (16/19) and 100% specificity (19/19) in the intention-to-test cohort, compared with 88.2% sensitivity (15/17) and 100% specificity (17/17) among technically evaluable samples. Three activating KRAS variants (L19F, A59T, and A146T) lay outside the tissue assays' target regions; patients carrying these alterations received anti-EGFR therapy. Patients with metastases in two or more organs had more detectable oncogenic alterations than those with one metastatic site (median, three versus two; adjusted q = 0.00184; rank-biserial correlation = 0.687). Serial sampling revealed divergent trajectories of individual variants in nine patients. Early reductions in plasma variant allele frequencies tended to be greater among partial responders, although associations with radiological response were not significant after multiple testing correction. Compact tumor-agnostic plasma sequencing provides complementary molecular information, but its clinical utility requires further validation.

item.title: The Immune-Nanomedicine Axis in Glioblastoma: From Biomimetic Delivery to Immune Reprogramming.
item.abstract: The therapeutic efficacy against glioblastoma (GBM) remains strictly limited by the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and the profoundly immunosuppressive network of the tumor microenvironment. To overcome these barriers, nanomedicine has shifted from conventional cytotoxin delivery toward the active functional reprogramming of the GBM immune microenvironment. Unlike existing literature that predominantly catalogues nanomaterial properties, this review maps the emerging immune-nanomedicine axis, focusing on recent preclinical proof-of-concept studies to decode how engineered platforms actively reprogram specific cellular compartments within this pathological niche. We evaluate nanoplatforms that utilize biomimetic camouflage and cellular hitchhiking to bypass the BBB and repolarize the myeloid stroma, as well as macroscopic implantable scaffolds designed to immunologically remodel the postoperative resection cavity. To link these innate responses to adaptive immunity, we discuss localized priming niches engineered to rescue dendritic cell cross-presentation. Furthermore, we examine interventions targeting T cell exhaustion-specifically metabolic checkpoint disruption, metalloimmunotherapy, and modalities that synchronize systemic mobilization with deep stromal infiltration. Finally, we review biomimetic and living-cell engineering strategies deployed to direct natural killer cells into the hypoxic tumor parenchyma. Despite robust preclinical data, clinical translation is fundamentally bottlenecked by the scalable manufacturing of complex nanomaterials, severe off-target neuroimmunological toxicities, and inherent physiological constraints of the host. Overcoming these hurdles demands structural minimalism and strict spatiotemporal precision. Ultimately, integrating synthetic biology with advanced 3D microfluidic models provides a necessary framework to bridge the gap between current preclinical achievements and future clinical viability.

item.title: Strain-associated variation in extracellular chemical profiles of fruit-derived Lactiplantibacillus plantarum under standardized cultivation.
item.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Lactiplantibacillus plantarum exhibits substantial strain-level metabolic diversity, yet comparative information on extracellular chemical profiles among fruit-derived strains remains limited.
METHODS: This study characterized and compared cell-free supernatants from five native fruit-derived L. plantarum strains cultivated under standardized conditions, using three independent biological cultures per strain. Untargeted LC-MS/MS profiling using RP-HSS T3 chromatography in positive- and negative-ion electrospray modes and HILIC-BEH Amide chromatography in negative-ion mode yielded 8,692 analytical detections, of which 6,769 had associated MS/MS information. Following annotation-confidence filtering, quality-control assessment, and consolidation across analytical configurations, 999 higher-confidence metabolite annotations (Levels 1a and 1b) were retained for comparative analysis.
RESULTS: Multivariate analyses revealed strain-associated differences in extracellular chemical profiles, with the extent of separation varying among strains. Welch's one-way ANOVA followed by Benjamini-Hochberg correction identified 438 of the 999 higher-confidence annotations as significantly different among strains (FDR < 0.05). Pairwise Welch's t-tests with FDR correction and |log2FC| ≥ 1 revealed strongly comparison-dependent differentiation; among comparisons centered on G1, 4, 39, 62, and 18 FDR-supported annotations were identified for G1 vs. G2, G1 vs. G3, G1 vs. G4, and G1 vs. G5, respectively. Comparison with an incubated uninoculated MRS control showed that part of the extracellular chemical background was also detectable in the cultivation medium; consequently, compounds detected in the cell-free supernatants were not attributed exclusively to bacterial biosynthesis.
CONCLUSION: These findings demonstrate substantial strain-associated variation in the extracellular chemical profiles of fruit-derived L. plantarum under standardized cultivation conditions and show that extracellular differentiation involves comparison-specific combinations of metabolite annotations rather than a uniform discriminatory signature. The higher-confidence candidates identified provide a basis for subsequent targeted quantitative and functional investigation of strain-associated extracellular phenotypes.

item.title: Mesenchymal Stem Cell-Derived Exosomes for Bone Regeneration: Modification Strategies and miRNA-Mediated Modulation of Osteogenic Signaling.
item.abstract: Bone tissue regeneration remains a major clinical challenge, and exosomes secreted by mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) have emerged as attractive cell-free therapeutic tools. To enhance their efficacy and local action, exosomes can be modified to enrich them with regulatory factors and impregnated into biocompatible matrices. This review summarizes recent advances in engineering MSC-derived exosomes for bone regeneration. Strategies analyzed include physicochemical modification of donor MSCs, direct exosome modification, and genetic modification of MSCs to enrich exosomes with therapeutic molecules such as bone morphogenetic protein 2 (BMP-2), vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), and regulatory miRNAs. In addition, the role of these miRNAs in osteogenic signaling was analyzed. Modified exosomes demonstrate enhanced osteogenic, angiogenic, and immunomodulatory effects in vitro and in vivo, particularly when combined with biomaterial scaffolds for sustained release. Thus, engineered MSC-derived exosomes constitute an effective approach for bone tissue engineering and show potential for clinical translation.

item.title: GelMA hydrogel enhances diabetic wound healing by delivering shock wave-preconditioned BMSC-derived small extracellular vesicles.
item.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) are chronic, hard-to-heal wounds characterized by impaired angiogenesis, persistent inflammation, and defective extracellular matrix remodeling. Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cell-derived small extracellular vesicles (BMSC-sEVs) hold promise for cell-free therapy; however, their therapeutic efficacy is limited by insufficient reparative bioactivity and rapid local clearance. This study aimed to enhance the intrinsic therapeutic potential of BMSC-sEVs through shock wave preconditioning and improve their local retention and sustained delivery using gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA) hydrogel.
METHODS: BMSCs were preconditioned with shock waves, and the resulting small extracellular vesicles (SW-sEVs) were isolated and characterized. Their angiogenic and immunomodulatory effects were evaluated using human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) and RAW264.7 macrophages. Proteomic analysis and Western blotting were performed to investigate potential underlying mechanisms. SW-sEVs were subsequently incorporated into a 15% GelMA hydrogel, and the resulting delivery system was characterized. Its therapeutic efficacy was evaluated in a streptozotocin (STZ)-induced hyperglycemic rat wound model.
RESULTS: Shock wave preconditioning did not alter the typical morphology, particle size distribution, or marker protein expression of BMSC-sEVs. Compared with sEVs derived from untreated BMSCs, SW-sEVs significantly enhanced HUVEC proliferation, migration, and tube formation, accompanied by increased VEGFA and CD31 expression. SW-sEVs also suppressed pro-inflammatory macrophage activation, promoted a reparative macrophage phenotype, and reduced the expression of pro-inflammatory factors. Proteomic analysis revealed alterations in sEV protein cargo, with differentially expressed proteins enriched in inflammation-related pathways, including NF-κB signaling. Western blotting further demonstrated reduced phosphorylation of p65 and IκBα following SW-sEV treatment. The 15% GelMA hydrogel exhibited an interconnected porous structure, favorable cytocompatibility, structural stability, and sustained SW-sEV release. In vivo, GelMA-SW-sEVs significantly accelerated diabetic wound healing, enhanced neovascularization and M2 macrophage polarization, reduced local inflammation, and improved re-epithelialization, collagen deposition, and tissue remodeling.
DISCUSSION: Shock wave preconditioning enhances the angiogenic and immunomodulatory activities of BMSC-sEVs, potentially through modulation of NF-κB-related inflammatory signaling. Combined with sustained local delivery using GelMA hydrogel, SW-sEVs demonstrate promising therapeutic potential as a cell-free strategy for diabetic wound repair.

item.title: From Bioprocess Design to Bioactivity: a new platform for antimicrobial-producing lactic acid bacteria.
item.abstract: Lactic acid bacteria (LAB) produce antimicrobial compounds with potential applications as natural food preservatives and alternatives to conventional antibiotics. However, their industrial use is limited by the high cost of conventional culture media and inefficient downstream recovery. This study developed an integrated, scalable, and cost-effective bioprocess for producing and recovering antibacterial metabolites from four LAB strains: Lactiplantibacillus plantarum, Limosilactobacillus reuteri, Lacticaseibacillus paracasei, and Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus. Culture medium optimization, fermentation intensification, and membrane-based downstream processing were investigated. Fed-batch cultivation achieved approximately three-fold higher biomass and secreted protein production than batch fermentation. Cell-free broths were processed by sequential ultrafiltration/diafiltration using 10 and 2 kDa membranes to obtain bacteriocin-enriched fractions. These fractions exhibited strong antimicrobial activity against selected skin and intestinal pathogens, reducing viable counts by up to 7-8 Log₁₀ CFU/mL. The proposed bioprocess provides a promising basis for the future scale-up of LAB-derived antibacterial peptides production for food and health applications.
